title: Authorization Evidence Handoff and Escalation Playbook
author: Priya Shah
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the standard process for assembling, validating, and handing off authorization (RBAC) and residency-related audit evidence to compliance reviewers and incident responders. It covers trigger conditions, artifact templates, SLAs, escalation paths, and an exceptions workflow for cases where evidence cannot be produced within the standard window.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference services and control planes (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Includes RBAC role assignments, privileged role rotations, access-request logs, audit trails from KMS/HSM, and data residency/retention manifests.
- Not intended for customer-specific contractual negotiations (handled by Legal/RevenueOps).

Definitions and key SLAs:
- Evidence collection SLA: 48 hours for standard requests, 24 hours for high-priority incident-driven requests.
- Audit log retention baseline: 365 days for control-plane logs, 730 days for payment/auth events (where mandated).
- Proof-of-access window: all role assignment events must be exportable for any 90-day window on request.

Owners and roles:
- Requestor: Product or Ops engineer who initiates an evidence request.
- Evidence Collector: Oncall or SRE assigned in the request (security owns coordination).
- Compliance Reviewer: Security Compliance PM (primary reviewer).
- Incident Responder: Eng-sre or Security IR lead for incidents.
- Exception Approver: Head of Security or delegated compliance lead.

Trigger scenarios (examples):
1) Routine audit: Quarterly compliance review for region X.
2) Customer audit: Customer requests proof of data residency and access controls.
3) Incident: Suspected unauthorized access or data exfiltration.
4) Internal exceptions: Change that bypassed standard approvals (emergency access).

Artifact catalog (what to gather):
- RBAC manifest: exported list of roles, role-bindings, effective principals, and start/expiry timestamps. Format: YAML (see example below).
- Access-change log: time-ordered CSV/JSON of grant/revoke events with actor, justification, and ticket ID.
- Privileged-session traces: pii-redacted shell session logs, jump-bastion records, and session duration.
- Audit-index: pointer file (JSON) mapping artifact locations (S3 path, retention tag, checksum).
- Residency manifest: bucket/region mapping, encryption-at-rest metadata, and KMS key IDs.
- Evidence provenance: collection timestamp, collector identity, hash, and collection method.

RBAC manifest example (YAML):
---
roles:
  - name: infra-admin
    id: role-23cd
    scope: org:infra
    bindings:
      - principal: user:anne.redwood@company.com
        assigned_at: 2025-10-01T09:12:33Z
        expires_at: 2026-01-01T09:12:33Z
      - principal: service:ci-bot@redwood
        assigned_at: 2025-11-08T02:00:00Z
    privileged: true

Access-change export (CLI examples):
- Export role bindings for a 90-day window (GCP/AWS examples shown):
  aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /redwood/iam --start-time 1700000000000 --end-time 1707776000000 --filter-pattern "PutRolePolicy" > access_changes_90d.json
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gce_instance" AND protoPayload.methodName:"SetIamPolicy"' --start-time=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z --end-time=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --format=json > access_changes_90d_gcp.json

Data residency manifest template (ASCII table):
| Resource path | Region | Encryption | KMS Key ID | Retention days |
| /s3/redwood-prod/logs | us-west-2 | AES256 | arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd | 730 |
| /gcs/redwood-prod/embeddings | europe-west1 | CMEK | projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/ek1 | 365 |

Evidence collection procedure (step-by-step):
1. Requestor files an evidence request in the Compliance queue (Jira ticket type: COMPL-EVID) with scope, time window, and reason.
2. Security triage: Within 4 business hours the Security Triage lead assigns an Evidence Collector and marks priority (standard / expedited).
3. Collector performs scoped exports using approved tooling (see approved-export-tools below), stamps each artifact with collection metadata, and uploads to the evidence S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<ticket-id>/.
4. Collector populates the Audit-index JSON and attaches it to the Jira ticket.
5. Compliance Reviewer verifies artifacts, requests clarifications if needed, and marks the ticket resolved or escalates.

Approved-export-tools and locations:
- rdb-audit-export (internal CLI) — outputs compressed JSON and attaches checksums.
- kubectl audit-exporter — for k8s RBAC events.
- redwood-log-archiver (internal) — for centralized audit log slices.
- Evidence storage: s3://redwood-evidence (access limited to compliance+security roles via bucket policy).

Validation checklist (minimum):
- [ ] RBAC manifest covers requested time window.
- [ ] All role-change events contain actor and justification.
- [ ] Residency manifest lists all storage resources and their regions.
- [ ] KMS key IDs present and match key registry.
- [ ] Checksums included and validated after upload.
- [ ] Evidence-index.json present in S3 and attached to ticket.

Escalation and exception flow:
- If evidence cannot be produced within the SLA due to log-rotation or retention limits, the Evidence Collector must:
  1. Immediately escalate to the Security Triage lead with reasons and available partial artifacts.
  2. Open an Exception Request (ticket labels: EXCEPTION / AUTH-EVID) with recommended mitigation (e.g., extended retention, rehydration from cold storage).
  3. Exception Approver has 72 hours to approve or require alternative evidence.
- Emergency incident path: If incident responders require evidence for an active breach, Security may invoke expedited collection and short-term emergency access to archived logs (must be recorded and approved post-facto).

Integration with Incident Response:
- Incident responders subscribe to evidence queue; any COMPL-EVID ticket linked to an active incident must be marked with incident ID and prioritized.
- For PII/SEV incidents, collectors must produce redacted artifacts and a redaction map describing removed fields.
- Chain-of-custody: For evidence used in legal or regulatory proceedings, the Collector must collect under the legal hold process and notify Legal immediately.

Common exception scenarios and mitigations (examples):
- Missing historical logs: Mitigate by retrieving from Glacier/Cold archives (may take 24–72 hours). Document retrieval ETA in ticket.
- Encrypted events missing keys: Coordinate with KMS team to (a) check key rotation logs, (b) verify key escrow policies.
- Cross-region exports blocked by network policy: Use staging export host in target region (requires temporary egress exception).

Runbook: Requesting an RBAC exception (step process):
1. Submit COMPL-EVID / EXCEPTION ticket with: affected role, time box, business justification, and risk assessment.
2. Security Triage performs quick risk assessment (<= 8 hours) and assigns temporary mitigations (e.g., scope-limited sessions, additional monitoring).
3. Exception Approver signs off or rejects. Approved exceptions must include compensating controls and a maximum duration (<= 14 days unless renewed).
4. All approved exceptions are recorded in the Exceptions Register (s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/registry.csv).

Checklist: Audit Evidence Package (final deliverable contents):
- Audit-index.json (string map of artifacts)
- RBAC manifest (YAML)
- Access-change export (CSV/JSON)
- Residency manifest (ASCII table or YAML)
- Checksums and provenance file (SHA256)
- Approval logs (ticket history, exception approvals)

Retention and archival policy references:
- Evidence artifacts follow the Evidence Retention policy: evidence-retention-policy-v2 (see product-docs) — default 7 years for high-risk events.
- Short-term exports kept in s3://redwood-evidence/temp/ with auto-delete: 30 days.

Auditability and tooling notes:
- All evidence collection actions must be logged in the collection audit stream (internal topic: audit.collection.events) with fields: collector, ticket_id, timestamp, artifact_path, checksum.
- Periodic validation job (monthly) re-hashes a random sample of artifacts and reports mismatches to the Compliance channel.
- Example validation SQL (run on the audit-index dataset):
  SELECT ticket_id, COUNT(artifact_path) AS artifacts, MAX(collected_at) AS last_collected
  FROM evidence_index
  WHERE collected_at >= '2025-01-01'
  GROUP BY ticket_id
  HAVING artifacts < 3;

References and related pages:
- Exceptions register: s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/registry.csv
- Evidence retention policy: product-docs/evidence-retention-policy-v2
- KMS rotation playbook: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/privileged-role-rotation-and-certification-guideline-2025.json

Appendix A — Example evidence-index.json (schema summary):
- ticket_id: string
- artifacts: list[string] (S3 paths)
- collector: string (email)
- collected_at: timestamp
- checksum: string (sha256)

Appendix B — Quick troubleshooting tips:
- If export tooling fails with "permission denied": verify export role in IAM; temporarily escalate to infra-admin using Emergency Access Flow and record in ticket.
- If checksum mismatch after upload: re-export artifact, re-calc checksum locally, and update evidence-index with new hash; notify Compliance Reviewer.

Contact information:
- Security Triage Slack: #sec-triage (monitored 24/7)
- Compliance mailbox: compliance@redwood.com
- Evidence storage owner: infra-storage@redwood.com

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Security (Priya Shah). Review cadence: annual or after any incident that invokes this playbook.

Change log:
- 2026-01-12: Initial published version.
- 2026-02-10: Clarified SLAs for incident-driven evidence and added audit-index schema summary.
